requirements.name: parse-toml-v1-spec
requirements.text: Build a TOML v1.0.0 parser that conforms to the specification in `sources/toml-v1.0.0.md`.

requirements.name: pass-full-suite
requirements.text: The goal is to pass every valid and every invalid case the installed suite supplies, with no case failed, errored, or skipped.

requirements.name: reject-invalid-input
requirements.text: Rejecting invalid input is scored as heavily as accepting valid input.

requirements.name: filter-stdin-stdout
requirements.text: The program is a filter: read TOML from **stdin**, write tagged JSON to **stdout**, exit `0`.

requirements.name: diagnose-invalid-toml
requirements.text: On invalid TOML, write a diagnostic to **stderr** and exit non-zero.

requirements.name: no-args-no-side-effects
requirements.text: The program takes no arguments, reads no configuration files, and produces no side effects.

requirements.name: tagged-json-value-encoding
requirements.text: Every TOML **value** becomes `{"type": "<TOML_TYPE>", "value": "<TOML_VALUE>"}`.

requirements.name: values-always-json-strings
requirements.text: `TOML_VALUE` is always a JSON string, including for integers, floats, and booleans.

requirements.name: empty-tables-encode-as-objects
requirements.text: Empty tables become `{}`.

requirements.name: offset-datetimes-rfc3339
requirements.text: Offset datetimes are encoded as RFC 3339.

requirements.name: parser-in-internal-package
requirements.text: The parser lives in `internal/toml`; `main` reads, delegates, and encodes.

requirements.name: scalars
requirements.text: booleans, integers (including `0x`, `0o`, `0b`, underscores), floats (including `inf`, `nan`, exponents).

requirements.name: string-forms
requirements.text: basic and literal strings, then multi-line strings with their line-ending backslash and trimming rules.

requirements.name: key-forms
requirements.text: bare, quoted, and dotted keys; the redefinition rules.

requirements.name: table-forms
requirements.text: `[table]`, `[a.b.c]` implicit creation, `[[array of tables]]`, and the rules governing which of these may follow which.

requirements.name: inline-tables-and-arrays
requirements.text: Inline tables and arrays — including nesting and the TOML 1.0 restriction that inline tables are closed to later extension.

requirements.name: datetime-forms
requirements.text: offset, local datetime, local date, local time.

requirements.name: reject-malformed-input
requirements.text: control characters, bad UTF-8, duplicate keys, redefinition after an inline table, unterminated constructs.

requirements.name: decoder-scaffolding
requirements.text: line handling, comments, whitespace, the stdin/stdout/exit contract, tagged JSON emission.

requirements.name: scoring-assets-read-only
requirements.text: The scoring assets are read-only.

requirements.name: build-decoder-command
requirements.text: Build `cmd/toml-decoder` so that the supplied entry point succeeds; changing the entry point is not a repair.

requirements.name: stdlib-only-module
requirements.text: `go.mod` declares no `require` dependencies.

requirements.name: no-network-after-setup
requirements.text: No network access at test time after `setup_harness.sh` has run once.

requirements.name: single-scoring-entry-point
requirements.text: `sources/full_test.sh` is the single scoring entry point.

requirements.name: clean-run-zero-exit
requirements.text: `sh sources/full_test.sh` runs cleanly with zero errors and exits zero.

requirements.name: build-decoder-command
requirements.text: go build -o toml-decoder ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: pin-toml-test-version
requirements.text: The version setup_harness.sh installs. run_conformance.sh refuses a different one, so a passing verdict names a specific exam rather than whichever harness was on PATH.

requirements.name: run-unfiltered-conformance
requirements.text: scoring entry point. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.

requirements.name: run-suite-against-decoder
requirements.text: Run the upstream toml-test conformance suite against the built decoder.

requirements.name: require-decoder-command
requirements.text: DECODER    decoder command. Required — this harness is language-neutral and deliberately has no default implementation language.

requirements.name: exit-status-standard
requirements.text: Exit code follows the harness exit-status standard in prompts/UAT_SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md: 0 only when every test passes, 2 when this harness could not run at all, and any other nonzero when it ran and the decoder failed. A precondition of the harness is never charged to the build.

requirements.name: locate-harness-binary
requirements.text: TOML_TEST  absolute path to the toml-test binary (default: found on PATH)

requirements.name: pin-suite-version
requirements.text: The suite's identity is part of the verdict. Without this, "the authoritative suite passed" names no particular suite: whichever toml-test happened to be on PATH decided the run, and a different version on a different machine is a different exam. Recorded always, and enforced when the caller states which version it expects.

requirements.name: forward-suite-arguments
requirements.text: DECODER=./toml-decoder sh sources/run_conformance.sh -run 'valid/string/*'  # one group

requirements.name: install-pinned-toml-test-harness
requirements.text: One-time installation of the upstream toml-test conformance harness.

requirements.name: architecture-boundary
requirements.text:
if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*require[[:space:](]' go.mod; then
  echo "go.mod declares a forbidden third-party dependency" >&2
  exit 1
fi
go build ./cmd/toml-decoder

requirements.name: decode-integer-assignment
reject-malformed-toml
requirements.text:
if printf 'answer = [\n' | ./toml-decoder >"$stage_dir/invalid.out" 2>"$stage_dir/invalid.err"; then
  echo "malformed TOML exited successfully" >&2
  exit 1
fi
test ! -s "$stage_dir/invalid.out"
test -s "$stage_dir/invalid.err"

requirements.name: run-story-slice
requirements.text: Same contract as full_test.sh, scoped to the cases a single story owns: build the decoder, then run the installed toml-test suite over the pattern given as $1.

requirements.name: verdict-is-exit-status
requirements.text: Exit status is the verdict and the whole verdict. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.

requirements.name: pin-suite-version
requirements.text: TOML_TEST_VERSION="${TOML_TEST_VERSION:-v2.2.0}"

requirements.name: case-sensitive
requirements.text: TOML is case-sensitive.

requirements.name: utf8-document
requirements.text: A TOML file must be a valid UTF-8 encoded Unicode document.

requirements.name: whitespace-and-newline
requirements.text:
Whitespace means tab (0x09) or space (0x20).
Newline means LF (0x0A) or CRLF (0x0D 0x0A).

requirements.name: comment-marker
requirements.text: A hash symbol marks the rest of the line as a comment, except when inside a string.

requirements.name: comment-control-characters
requirements.text:
Control characters other than tab (U+0000 to U+0008, U+000A to U+001F, U+007F)
are not permitted in comments.

requirements.name: key-value-pair
requirements.text: Keys are on the left of the equals sign and values are on the right. Whitespace is ignored around key names and values. The key, equals sign, and value must be on the same line (though some values can be broken over multiple lines).

requirements.name: key-value-line-end
requirements.text: There must be a newline (or EOF) after a key/value pair.

requirements.name: values-typed
requirements.text:
Values must have one of the following types.
Unspecified values are invalid.

requirements.name: maps-to-hash-table
requirements.text: TOML is designed to map unambiguously to a hash table.

requirements.name: bare-keys
requirements.text: Bare keys may only contain ASCII letters, ASCII digits, underscores, and dashes (`A-Za-z0-9_-`).

requirements.name: bare-keys-digits-are-strings
requirements.text: Note that bare keys are allowed to be composed of only ASCII digits, e.g. `1234`, but are always interpreted as strings.

requirements.name: quoted-keys
requirements.text: Quoted keys follow the exact same rules as either basic strings or literal strings and allow you to use a much broader set of key names.

requirements.name: empty-keys
requirements.text: A bare key must be non-empty, but an empty quoted key is allowed (though discouraged).

requirements.name: dotted-keys
requirements.text: Dotted keys are a sequence of bare or quoted keys joined with a dot.

requirements.name: dotted-key-whitespace
requirements.text: Whitespace around dot-separated parts is ignored.

requirements.name: key-defined-once
requirements.text: Defining a key multiple times is invalid.

requirements.name: bare-and-quoted-keys-equivalent
requirements.text: Note that bare keys and quoted keys are equivalent:

requirements.name: dotted-key-extension
requirements.text: As long as a key hasn't been directly defined, you may still write to it and to names within it.

requirements.name: dotted-keys-out-of-order
requirements.text: Defining dotted keys out-of-order is discouraged.

requirements.name: dotted-keys-float-lookalike
requirements.text: Since bare keys can be composed of only ASCII integers, it is possible to write dotted keys that look like floats but are 2-part dotted keys.

requirements.name: indentation-ignored
requirements.text: Indentation is treated as whitespace and ignored.

requirements.name: string-basic
requirements.text: Basic strings are surrounded by quotation marks (`"`). Any Unicode character may be used except those that must be escaped: quotation mark, backslash, and the control characters other than tab (U+0000 to U+0008, U+000A to U+001F, U+007F).

requirements.name: string-compact-escapes
requirements.text: For convenience, some popular characters have a compact escape sequence.

requirements.name: string-unicode-escapes
requirements.text: Any Unicode character may be escaped with the `\uXXXX` or `\UXXXXXXXX` forms. The escape codes must be valid Unicode scalar values.

requirements.name: string-reserved-escapes
requirements.text: All other escape sequences not listed above are reserved; if they are used, TOML should produce an error.

requirements.name: string-multiline-basic
requirements.text: Multi-line basic strings are surrounded by three quotation marks on each side and allow newlines. A newline immediately following the opening delimiter will be trimmed. All other whitespace and newline characters remain intact.

requirements.name: string-newline-normalization
requirements.text: TOML parsers should feel free to normalize newline to whatever makes sense for their platform.

requirements.name: string-line-ending-backslash
requirements.text: When the last non-whitespace character on a line is an unescaped `\`, it will be trimmed along with all whitespace (including newlines) up to the next non-whitespace character or closing delimiter.

requirements.name: string-multiline-basic-quotes
requirements.text: You can write a quotation mark, or two adjacent quotation marks, anywhere inside a multi-line basic string.

requirements.name: string-multiline-basic-control-characters
requirements.text: Any Unicode character may be used except those that must be escaped: backslash and the control characters other than tab, line feed, and carriage return (U+0000 to U+0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E to U+001F, U+007F).

requirements.name: string-literal
requirements.text: Literal strings are surrounded by single quotes. Like basic strings, they must appear on a single line.

requirements.name: string-multiline-literal
requirements.text: Multi-line literal strings are surrounded by three single quotes on each side and allow newlines. Like literal strings, there is no escaping whatsoever. A newline immediately following the opening delimiter will be trimmed. All other content between the delimiters is interpreted as-is without modification.

requirements.name: string-multiline-literal-quote-limit
requirements.text: You can write 1 or 2 single quotes anywhere within a multi-line literal string, but sequences of three or more single quotes are not permitted.

requirements.name: string-literal-control-characters
requirements.text: Control characters other than tab are not permitted in a literal string.

requirements.name: integer-forms
requirements.text: Integers are whole numbers. Positive numbers may be prefixed with a plus sign. Negative numbers are prefixed with a minus sign.

requirements.name: integer-underscores
requirements.text: For large numbers, you may use underscores between digits to enhance readability. Each underscore must be surrounded by at least one digit on each side.

requirements.name: integer-leading-zeros
requirements.text: Leading zeros are not allowed. Integer values `-0` and `+0` are valid and identical to an unprefixed zero.

requirements.name: integer-radix-prefixes
requirements.text: Non-negative integer values may also be expressed in hexadecimal, octal, or binary. In these formats, leading `+` is not allowed and leading zeros are allowed (after the prefix).

requirements.name: integer-64-bit-range
requirements.text: Arbitrary 64-bit signed integers (from −2^63 to 2^63−1) should be accepted and handled losslessly. If an integer cannot be represented losslessly, an error must be thrown.

requirements.name: float-ieee-binary64
requirements.text: Floats should be implemented as IEEE 754 binary64 values.

requirements.name: float-structure
requirements.text: A float consists of an integer part (which follows the same rules as decimal integer values) followed by a fractional part and/or an exponent part. If both a fractional part and exponent part are present, the fractional part must precede the exponent part.

requirements.name: float-fractional-part
requirements.text: A fractional part is a decimal point followed by one or more digits. The decimal point, if used, must be surrounded by at least one digit on each side.

requirements.name: float-exponent-part
requirements.text: An exponent part is an E (upper or lower case) followed by an integer part (which follows the same rules as decimal integer values but may include leading zeros).

requirements.name: float-underscores
requirements.text: Similar to integers, you may use underscores to enhance readability. Each underscore must be surrounded by at least one digit.

requirements.name: float-signed-zero
requirements.text: Float values `-0.0` and `+0.0` are valid and should map according to IEEE 754.

requirements.name: float-special-values
requirements.text: Special float values can also be expressed. They are always lowercase.

requirements.name: boolean
requirements.text: Booleans are just the tokens you're used to. Always lowercase.

requirements.name: offset-datetime
requirements.text: To unambiguously represent a specific instant in time, you may use an RFC 3339 formatted date-time with offset.

requirements.name: datetime-space-separator
requirements.text: For the sake of readability, you may replace the T delimiter between date and time with a space character (as permitted by RFC 3339 section 5.6).

requirements.name: datetime-fractional-precision
requirements.text: Millisecond precision is required. Further precision of fractional seconds is implementation-specific. If the value contains greater precision than the implementation can support, the additional precision must be truncated, not rounded.

requirements.name: local-datetime
requirements.text: If you omit the offset from an RFC 3339 formatted date-time, it will represent the given date-time without any relation to an offset or timezone.

requirements.name: local-date
requirements.text: If you include only the date portion of an RFC 3339 formatted date-time, it will represent that entire day without any relation to an offset or timezone.

requirements.name: local-time
requirements.text: If you include only the time portion of an RFC 3339 formatted date-time, it will represent that time of day without any relation to a specific day or any offset or timezone.

requirements.name: array-values
requirements.text: Arrays are square brackets with values inside. Whitespace is ignored. Elements are separated by commas. Arrays can contain values of the same data types as allowed in key/value pairs. Values of different types may be mixed.

requirements.name: array-multiline
requirements.text: Arrays can span multiple lines. A terminating comma (also called a trailing comma) is permitted after the last value of the array. Any number of newlines and comments may precede values, commas, and the closing bracket. Indentation between array values and commas is treated as whitespace and ignored.

requirements.name: inline-table-syntax
requirements.text: Inline tables are fully defined within curly braces: `{` and `}`. Within the braces, zero or more comma-separated key/value pairs may appear. Key/value pairs take the same form as key/value pairs in standard tables. All value types are allowed, including inline tables.

requirements.name: inline-table-single-line
requirements.text: Inline tables are intended to appear on a single line. A terminating comma (also called trailing comma) is not permitted after the last key/value pair in an inline table. No newlines are allowed between the curly braces unless they are valid within a value.

requirements.name: inline-table-closed
requirements.text: Inline tables are fully self-contained and define all keys and sub-tables within them. Keys and sub-tables cannot be added outside the braces.

requirements.name: inline-table-no-extension
requirements.text: Similarly, inline tables cannot be used to add keys or sub-tables to an already-defined table.

requirements.name: table-headers
requirements.text: Tables (also known as hash tables or dictionaries) are collections of key/value pairs. They are defined by headers, with square brackets on a line by themselves.

requirements.name: table-scope
requirements.text: Under that, and until the next header or EOF, are the key/values of that table.

requirements.name: table-no-order
requirements.text: Key/value pairs within tables are not guaranteed to be in any specific order.

requirements.name: table-naming
requirements.text: Naming rules for tables are the same as for keys

requirements.name: table-whitespace
requirements.text: Whitespace around the key is ignored.

requirements.name: implicit-super-tables
requirements.text: You don't need to specify all the super-tables if you don't want to. TOML knows how to do it for you.

requirements.name: empty-tables
requirements.text: Empty tables are allowed and simply have no key/value pairs within them.

requirements.name: table-defined-once
requirements.text: Like keys, you cannot define a table more than once. Doing so is invalid.

requirements.name: tables-out-of-order
requirements.text: Defining tables out-of-order is discouraged.

requirements.name: root-table
requirements.text: The top-level table, also called the root table, starts at the beginning of the document and ends just before the first table header (or EOF). Unlike other tables, it is nameless and cannot be relocated.

requirements.name: dotted-keys-define-tables
requirements.text: Dotted keys create and define a table for each key part before the last one, provided that such tables were not previously created.

requirements.name: table-header-and-dotted-key-conflicts
requirements.text: Since tables cannot be defined more than once, redefining such tables using a `[table]` header is not allowed. Likewise, using dotted keys to redefine tables already defined in `[table]` form is not allowed. The `[table]` form can, however, be used to define sub-tables within tables defined via dotted keys.

requirements.name: array-of-tables
requirements.text: These can be expressed by using a header with a name in double brackets. The first instance of that header defines the array and its first table element, and each subsequent instance creates and defines a new table element in that array. The tables are inserted into the array in the order encountered.

requirements.name: array-of-tables-reference
requirements.text: Any reference to an array of tables points to the most recently defined table element of the array.

requirements.name: array-parent-defined-first
requirements.text: If the parent of a table or array of tables is an array element, that element must already have been defined before the child can be defined. Attempts to reverse that ordering must produce an error at parse time.

requirements.name: static-array-no-append
requirements.text: Attempting to append to a statically defined array, even if that array is empty, must produce an error at parse time.

requirements.name: table-array-conflict
requirements.text: Attempting to define a normal table with the same name as an already established array must produce an error at parse time. Attempting to redefine a normal table as an array must likewise produce a parse-time error.
